newsitem.title: GERMANY: GERMAN SHARES RECOVER COMPOSURE IN IBIS TRADE.
newsitem.headline: GERMAN SHARES RECOVER COMPOSURE IN IBIS TRADE.

text.p: The German share market recovered some composure in pre-bourse electronic trade on Thursday after turbulent late trade on Wednesday sent the DAX index spinning down, but lost ground as bourse trade neared.
The IBIS DAX index stood at 4,247.32 points, up 10.26 points or 0.24 percent, way off earlier highs of 4,290.25 points, while the September DAX future was up 16.5 points at 4,262.5.
"The market will move sideways until the U.S. data comes in later on," a trader said, referring to the rash of indicators coming from the United States from 1230 GMT on.
The data include weekly U.S. jobless claims, July consumer prices and industrial production.
Shares in the news included utility RWE AG, which said on Wednesday that it would abolish multiple voting rights on shares mainly held by local municipalities.
Preference shares in RWE were up 8.70 marks, or 13.14 percent, at 74.90 marks, while ordinary shares were up 6.95 marks, or 8.73 percent, at 86.60 marks.
Among the big corporate news of the morning were half-year results from chemical giant BASF AG.
BASF said net income in the first half of the year was up 3.4 percent at 1.417 billion marks, while sales were up 14.5 percent at 27.797 billion marks, at the lower end of analysts' expectations.
Shares in BASF were among the loss leaders pre-bourse, down 1.35 marks, or 1.89 percent, at 70.15 marks.
